title: Calendly Not Syncing with Google Calendar: How to Fix It
body_md:
![Calendly help page on connecting your Google Calendar](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/calendly-not-syncing-with-google-calendar-how-to-fix-it/1.png)
*Calendly's official How to connect your Google Calendar help page ([source](https://calendly.com/help/how-to-connect-your-google-calendar))*

## The Quick Fix

Go to **Settings → Scheduling → Calendars** in Calendly and check that the right calendars are selected under **Calendars to check for conflicts** — and that you've picked a destination under **Calendar to add events to**. That's the path in Calendly's own help docs: Settings → Scheduling → Calendars, then select which calendars to check under Calendars to check for conflicts and choose a calendar under Calendar to add events to. There's a second route to the same settings through Availability → Calendar settings, where you can also add a calendar account.

Then check whether the sub-calendar is actually ticked and whether the Google event is marked **Busy**. A Free event is invisible to Calendly; see [Calendly's unavailable-time guide](https://calendly.com/help/how-to-troubleshoot-unavailable-times-that-should-be-available).

## Why This Happens

Settings cause most of these problems, but outages happen too. Check the service status before you start rebuilding connections, then work through these possibilities:

- **The wrong sub-calendars are selected.** Calendly only blocks time from the calendars you explicitly check. Your "Personal" or "Family" calendar sitting under the same Google account won't count unless you select it.
- **Events are marked Free, not Busy.** Calendly marks you unavailable during busy events on the calendars you've selected, including all-day and multi-day events — so an event marked Free blocks nothing.
- **Shared-calendar access may need review.** Confirm the calendar is shared with the Google account connected to Calendly and appears in your calendar list. Check the exact access level needed with Calendly support for your setup. Don't automatically grant permission to manage sharing.
- **You changed sharing settings after connecting.** If sharing or calendar selections were updated after the initial connection, reconnecting the calendar often clears the glitch.
- **No destination calendar is set**, so booked meetings never write back to Google. You can only publish events to one connected calendar, so if you've connected more than one, you have to pick which gets the bookings.
- **Plan limits.** Calendly's plan comparison lists one calendar connection on Free and six on Standard, Teams and Enterprise — so a second or third account won't connect on a free plan.

## Step-by-Step Fixes

![Google Calendar Help homepage](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/calendly-not-syncing-with-google-calendar-how-to-fix-it/4.png)
*Google Calendar Help ([source](https://support.google.com/calendar))*

### 1. Verify your conflict-checking calendars (2 minutes)

Head to **Settings → Scheduling → Calendars**. If you signed up using a Google email address, your calendar may already be connected — if it's listed there, you're all set on that front.

Now look at the calendar list under the connected account and tick every sub-calendar that holds real commitments: Work, Personal, side-project, whatever. Unchecked calendars are invisible to Calendly.

Then confirm the **Calendar to add events to** field points at the calendar you actually live in. If bookings are "disappearing," they're often landing on a secondary calendar you never open.

### 2. Check the Free/Busy status of the events that got double-booked

Open one of the Google Calendar events Calendly ignored, click into the event details, and look at the availability setting. Set it to **Busy** and save. Refresh your Calendly booking page and confirm the slot is gone.

Recurring events keep their original setting, so if a weekly block was created as Free, every instance is invisible.

### 3. Fix sharing permissions on borrowed calendars

If the calendar belongs to another account, ask its owner or administrator to review access for the Google account connected to Calendly. Grant only the access needed for the job. **Make changes and manage sharing** also lets that account re-share the calendar, so it shouldn't be your default troubleshooting step. See [Google's calendar permission guidance](https://support.google.com/calendar/answer/15716974). Once access is confirmed, recheck Calendly's selected conflict calendars.

### 4. Disconnect and reconnect the calendar

This is the reset button, and it clears stale OAuth tokens and permission changes that never propagated. Disconnect Google Calendar in Calendly, clear your browser cache and cookies, restart the browser, then reconnect.

Use Connect next to Google Calendar for your first calendar, or + Connect calendar account then Google Calendar to add another, and sign in when prompted.

Reconnecting resets your selections. Re-check your sub-calendars and your destination calendar afterward, then book a test meeting with yourself to confirm the event lands in Google.

### 5. Confirm you haven't hit your plan's calendar limit

If a second Google account won't connect at all — or connects but never appears in the conflict list — you may be at your plan's cap. Calendly caps calendar connections at six across all tiers, including Enterprise, and the free plan is limited to one. Feature access can also vary with when your account was created and which add-ons you have, so check your current plan before assuming it's a bug.

### 6. Rule out event-type-level settings

Sometimes the calendar sync is fine and the event type is the culprit. Open the event type from your Scheduling page, go into More options, and review the availability rules — limits and buffers, free/busy rules, booking page options — then save and check your booking page. Buffers and daily meeting limits can make availability look broken when sync is working perfectly.

### 7. Contact support with specifics

If everything is connected and correct but events still aren't writing to Google, it's a backend issue. Reach out through in-app chat or Calendly support with the date, time, and invitee for a specific failed booking — vague reports get slow answers.

## How to Prevent It Next Time

- **Default new Google events to Busy.** Check your Google Calendar settings so newly created events aren't defaulting to Free.
- **Re-audit your calendar list after any change** — a new work account, a new sub-calendar, a password reset, a reconnect. Selections don't carry over automatically.
- **Run a monthly test booking.** Book yourself through your own public link and confirm the event appears in Google within a minute. It takes 30 seconds and catches silent failures before a client does.
- **Keep the destination calendar the same as a conflict-checked calendar.** That way every Calendly booking immediately blocks future availability instead of leaving a gap.
- **Don't stack too many calendar accounts.** Every extra connection is another place for permissions to break. Consolidate with sub-calendars under one Google account where you can.

*Updated October 2026: this guide is written from Calendly's and Google's official documentation and public user reports, not from a controlled diagnostic test.*

## My Take

My read is that "Calendly isn't syncing" is almost never a sync failure. It's a selection problem. Calendly reads the calendars you ticked and respects the Busy flag, and both of those are things a human changes and then forgets. The product isn't broken; the mental model is.

I think the Free/Busy default is the single most under-appreciated setting in this whole stack. People create a recurring focus block, set it Free so teammates can still grab them, and then wonder why strangers are booking over it every Tuesday. Fix the default once and you remove a whole category of future incidents.

The free plan's single calendar connection is the other quiet trap. One connection means one account — if you run work and personal Google accounts, the free tier structurally cannot see both, and no amount of reconnecting changes that. Standard is $10 per seat per month on annual billing, or $12 monthly, which is $24 more per year to pay monthly. If double-booking has already cost you one awkward client email, that math is easy.

Fair point for the other side: not every report is user error. Calendars are OAuth-dependent, tokens do go stale, and a disconnect-reconnect genuinely fixes things that no settings audit would catch. That's why step 4 exists rather than being a last resort.

What I'd actually do is make the monthly test booking non-negotiable. Every other fix here is reactive — you find out something broke because an invitee landed on top of your dentist appointment. A 30-second self-booking is the only step on this list that catches the failure before someone else does. I'm not a lawyer or an accountant, so if a missed booking has contractual or billing consequences on your end, take that part to someone who is.
